programs.name: Brass Swell I
programs.description: A rounded harmonic body enters before the brighter circuit rank completes its swell. The lip-like attack settles into a stable center; pressure opens the held chord and the wheel adds restrained vibrato.

programs.name: Brass Swell II
programs.description: A modeled 16' brass foundation supports an 8' circuit crown. Staggered filter rises broaden the swell while the darker lower spectrum preserves weight; pressure brings forward the upper rank.

programs.name: Pressure Swell Brass
programs.description: A quiet harmonic brass body waits under the fingers. Pressure supplies most of the level and brightens both the modeled body and the circuit edge; easing pressure returns to the soft bed.

programs.name: Resonant Swell Brass
programs.description: A warm circuit body rises ahead of a more focused resonant accent. The brighter peak relaxes sooner, keeping the sustained chord full without leaving a static nasal ring.

programs.name: Noir Swell Brass
programs.description: A dark circuit body opens slowly beneath a later luminous upper rank. Reduced chorus and a steadier pitch center leave the evolving filter bloom clear; pressure adds intensity and gentle vibrato.

programs.name: Sforzando Brass
programs.description: A bright brass attack relaxes rapidly into a quieter sustained harmonic body. The separate upper accent decays away, while velocity changes its spectral bite as well as its weight.

programs.name: Brass Stab
programs.description: A compact, dry brass hit with a shaped harmonic attack beneath a shorter circuit bite. Both ranks die away on a held key; tight key releases keep repeated chords distinct.

programs.name: Horn Section
programs.description: Two closely tuned harmonic brass ranks form a warm horn section. Their soft, staggered attacks and differently weighted upper harmonics give depth without a heavy chorus; pressure brings out the brass bloom.

programs.name: Covered Horn
programs.description: A dark, stable horn body with a restrained upper lip edge and rounded breath release. Pressure favors expressive level over brightness; the harmonic body remains clear through middle and lower-register phrasing.

programs.name: Muted Trumpet
programs.description: A compact, bright harmonic brass body meets a narrow nasal circuit edge. A quick tongue-like accent settles before the held note; pressure sharpens the focus and adds a small expressive vibrato.

programs.name: Trombone Glide
programs.description: A weighty 16' harmonic brass body follows a restrained lip scoop and smooth slide-like portamento. Its quieter edge rank speaks sooner, keeping low phrases articulate without chorus.

programs.name: Fanfare Brass
programs.description: An assertive 8' harmonic section carries a shorter 4' circuit crown. Velocity sharpens the lip-like onset, and the lighter octave settles quickly so the played root stays strong through the held chord.

programs.name: Brass Ensemble 16
programs.description: A weighty 16' harmonic foundation supports a later 8' brass section. Restrained chorus joins the differently voiced ranks while preserving the low center and their separate entrances.

programs.name: Low Brass
programs.description: Two 16' harmonic brass ranks combine a rounded low foundation with a smaller lip edge. A slower body attack and short breath-like release give weight to low phrases without continual pitch wobble.

programs.name: Velvet Brass
programs.description: A soft harmonic center supports a dark circuit halo that enters later. Shallow pulse movement and restrained chorus keep the long release smooth; pressure adds warmth and level without a sharp edge.

programs.name: Bright Brass Poly
programs.description: Fast circuit brass comping with a rounded sustaining center and a brief, bright upper accent. Greater attack contrast and a tighter upper release keep rhythmic chord changes clear.

programs.name: Brass Pad Swell
programs.description: A soft harmonic core takes over a second to rise while a later circuit rank completes the bright bloom. The upper section remains lighter during the long overlap, giving sustained chords depth and a clear center.

programs.name: Fifth Brass
programs.description: An 8' harmonic brass body carries a softly entering 5 1/3' circuit fifth. The fifth relaxes sooner and stays subordinate, preserving the played root in open chord voicings.

programs.name: Wah Brass
programs.description: A full circuit brass body acquires a rhythmic filter wah as pressure feeds the sine SUB into the VCF. Differently shaped rank envelopes preserve a warm center beneath the moving edge; the wheel adds a small vibrato.

programs.name: Synth Horns
programs.description: A firm saw body precedes a moving saw-and-pulse horn edge. Slower, shallower pulse motion and a shorter upper bloom keep the synth identity rich while reducing the static, buzzy blend.

programs.name: Brass Bite
programs.description: Soft strikes retain a rounded circuit body; hard strikes add a much shorter resonant upper bite. The accent drops away before the body, leaving pressure to shape the held bloom.

programs.name: Distant Brass
programs.description: A dark harmonic center supports a softened, later circuit section. Slower entrances and a long diffuse release suggest distance, while reduced chorus preserves chord pitch and the upper edge stays subdued.

programs.name: Brass Crescendo
programs.description: A harmonic brass body rises for 1.6 seconds before the brighter upper section completes the crescendo. Hold the chord through the opening, then use pressure to increase harmonic intensity without retriggering the entrance.

programs.name: Cuivre Brass
programs.description: A rounded harmonic brass body retains its root while pressure introduces a focused, overblown circuit edge. The upper lip-like accent settles quickly after the attack, leaving a responsive contrast between soft and forceful playing.

programs.name: Tuba
programs.description: A single dry 16' harmonic brass body with a deep fundamental and dark upper spectrum. A gentle tongue onset and compact breath release support low separated phrases; pressure adds weight without ensemble detuning.

programs.name: Brass Octaves
programs.description: Straight-tuned 8' and 4' brass ranks combine harmonic depth with a lighter circuit edge. The upper octave speaks slightly later and settles lower, remaining present without competing with the root.

programs.name: Swell And Fall
programs.description: A warm harmonic-supported brass swell becomes darker after key release. The brighter circuit rank opens later and falls away sooner, producing a deliberate rise and closing gesture instead of a static pad tail.

programs.name: Reed Brass
programs.description: A stable harmonic brass body combines with a narrow reed-colored upper rank. Their staggered attacks and different pressure response let the reed edge emerge expressively without replacing the brass foundation.

programs.name: Brass Glide Lead
programs.description: A centered harmonic brass lead follows a small upward scoop and smooth portamento. A softer circuit edge enters behind the body, while pressure supplies brightness and restrained vibrato for a single focused line.

programs.name: Tremolo Brass
programs.description: A soft harmonic-supported brass pad pulses gently at 4.6 Hz through the original SUB VCA route. The later, lighter circuit rank and restrained stereo tremolo preserve a rounded center through the motion.

programs.name: Contour Brass
programs.description: A broad harmonic brass body and lighter circuit crown are balanced for wide keyboard voicings. A gentle brilliance contour and restrained treble level keep upper notes from becoming sharp while low chords retain their center.

programs.name: Ring Breath Brass
programs.description: A slow, shallow ring component shades a warm harmonic-supported chord. The lighter circuit rank opens later, and the ring motion emerges gently so held chords breathe without a hard amplitude pulse.

programs.name: Ensemble Strings
programs.description: A modeled bowed body enters before a lighter moving upper section. Different harmonic weights and restrained chorus give the ranks depth; pressure adds bow intensity and gentle vibrato.

programs.name: Slow Strings
programs.description: A soft bowed harmonic body rises over 0.85 seconds and the brighter section follows over 1.15 seconds. Hold the chord through the opening to hear their separate spectral blooms and long overlapping releases.

programs.name: Violins
programs.description: An 8' modeled bowed section carries a quieter 4' upper sheen. A quick bow onset, clear upper harmonics and restrained chorus preserve articulated lines, with pressure adding intensity after the attack.

programs.name: Cellos
programs.description: A larger 16' cello body supports a shorter 8' bow edge; its lower resonant bands remain distinct from the violin section. The darker low spectrum keeps weight beneath the articulation; pressure opens the upper harmonics without a broad ensemble wobble.

programs.name: Octave Strings
programs.description: An 8' harmonic bowed section is joined by a lighter, later 4' section. Different upper-partial weights and envelope timing keep both registers clear without hollowing the lower body.

programs.name: PWM Strings
programs.description: Two pulse sections evolve at distinct slow rates, with the second filter bloom arriving later. Reduced PWM excursion and chorus preserve a steady pitch center while the harmonic balance keeps moving.

programs.name: Thin Strings
programs.description: A high-passed circuit section retains a narrow upper-string texture without losing every low harmonic. The thinner second rank enters later and relaxes sooner, making the distant sound airy rather than brittle.

programs.name: Dark Strings
programs.description: A dark modeled bowed body supports covered pulse overtones. Slow harmonic openings and a restrained chorus keep the low center intact while the long releases join soft, sombre chords.

programs.name: Tremolo Strings
programs.description: A 6.5 Hz rounded level motion suggests repeated bow strokes across a sustained harmonic body. The lighter upper rank responds more quickly, keeping the tremolo animated without abrupt square-wave chopping.

programs.name: Solo Violin
programs.description: A dry 8' modeled bowed body carries evolving upper harmonics beneath a separate, brief bow-friction onset. Velocity shapes the bow and pressure adds controlled vibrato; the stable single line has no ensemble chorus.

programs.name: Solo Cello
programs.description: A dry 16' bowed body uses larger cello resonances while retaining its upper bow band. A warm fundamental follows an independently fading low bow-friction onset. Pressure adds weight and restrained vibrato, with no octave layer or ensemble chorus.

programs.name: Pizzicato Strings
programs.description: A plucked-string harmonic body follows a shorter upper pluck, with faster losses in the high partials as the note settles. Both ranks decay to silence on a held key; velocity changes the excitation and short release damps the strings.

programs.name: Swell Strings
programs.description: A quiet modeled bow bed gains harmonic weight and level under pressure. The lighter upper section enters later, and easing pressure returns the same held bow to a soft texture without retriggering.

programs.name: Chamber Strings
programs.description: Two closely tuned modeled bow sections speak at slightly different times without chorus. Distinct harmonic weights and restrained motion suggest a small group while preserving clear note changes.

programs.name: Wide Strings
programs.description: Broad stereo sections combine harmonic bowed depth with a moving pulse sheen. Reduced detuning and chorus preserve the pitch center while the slower upper entrance keeps sustained chords open.

programs.name: Crystal Strings
programs.description: An 8' harmonic bowed body supports a delicate 2' circuit glint. The upper register opens later and stays light, adding a glassy edge without overtaking the string center.

programs.name: Fifth Strings
programs.description: A softly entering harmonic fifth joins an 8' modeled bowed body. The fifth has a lighter spectral weight and remains subordinate through the release; sparse voicings reveal the open interval clearly.

programs.name: Analog Orchestra
programs.description: A warm 16' circuit section and a lighter 4' upper section span two octaves. Staggered harmonic blooms and reduced chorus keep the orchestral synth texture broad while preserving low-register definition.

programs.name: Spiccato Strings
programs.description: A firm modeled bow stroke decays into silence without held sustain. A quiet, shorter upper edge marks the attack; velocity shapes the excitation and level, and a quick key release separates detached notes.

programs.name: Bowed Swell Strings
programs.description: A modeled bow body rises before the two harmonic ranges bloom over 1.1 and 1.5 seconds. Hold the chord to hear the brighter section emerge, then use pressure to increase bow intensity without losing the covered center.

programs.name: Synth Strings Saw
programs.description: Two circuit saw sections bloom at different rates before settling into a covered synth-string sustain. Restrained chorus, a steadier tuning center and separate long releases keep the texture lush without a smeared attack.

programs.name: String Machine
programs.description: Bright circuit saw sections use a fast ensemble chorus, steady sustain and very little touch dependence. A stronger lower foundation, quicker first rank and controlled detuning keep rhythmic chord changes immediate.

programs.name: Contour Strings
programs.description: Modeled bow harmonics and a brighter circuit section share a keyboard contour. The low range stays soft while restrained treble brilliance and level keep wide voicings balanced across the keyboard.

programs.name: Ring Strings
programs.description: A quiet, slowly entering ring component adds level shimmer behind a harmonic-supported ensemble. The warmer center stays stable through the movement and long release, with no metallic fixed pitch imposed on the strings.

programs.name: Velvet Strings
programs.description: A soft modeled bowed body carries low pulse overtones with very shallow movement. Dark harmonic weighting and separately shaped long releases make a smooth, warm tail without a bright layer hovering above it.

programs.name: Tutti Strings
programs.description: A strong 16' modeled bow body supports an 8' section with brighter, faster-speaking harmonics. Moderate chorus joins the sections while velocity gives articulated chords a clear opening weight.

programs.name: Marcato Strings
programs.description: A firm upper bow burst decays into a quieter modeled harmonic body. Velocity shapes the bite and its weight; the independent accent disappears during the hold, leaving a clear sustained bow.

programs.name: Air Strings
programs.description: A modeled bowed body holds beneath a separate filtered friction layer. The air opens quickly and fades to a restrained breath, while pressure supports the pitched body and the release stays clean.

programs.name: Slow Pad
programs.description: A warm saw body fades in before a brighter moving pulse rank. Their filter blooms and release lengths overlap gently; pressure brings forward the upper color.

programs.name: Ring Drift Pad
programs.description: A steady low-mid body and lighter pulse halo move through a slow ring beat. The ring frequency envelope adds a gentle drift while the held pitch remains recognizable.

programs.name: Choir Pad
programs.description: Two softly voiced open-vowel bodies retain their vocal resonances across the keyboard. The upper choir enters later and remains lighter; pressure adds effort and upper color without moving the vowel bands with the played pitch.

programs.name: Dark Choir
programs.description: A covered oo vowel at 16 feet supports a lighter 8-foot choir. Vocal-body resonances stay in place as the notes change; unequal breath entrances and restrained upper effort preserve the dark ensemble color.

programs.name: Sweep Pad
programs.description: A sustained body opens over three seconds, followed by a higher pulse bloom. Hold beyond four seconds to hear both filter crests and their gradual settling.

programs.name: Breathing Pad
programs.description: A rounded pad gently swells and recedes at 0.7 Hz. The original SUB moves level by a few decibels while slower PWM keeps the upper rank alive.

programs.name: Glass Pad
programs.description: An 8' soft body supports a late 2' sine and pulse glint. The high rank has its own brighter filter and lower sustain, letting the glass color float above the chord.

programs.name: Warm Pad
programs.description: A filtered saw with a small sine foundation and a quiet soft-pulse companion. Compact stereo motion and modest pressure brightness preserve the warm center.

programs.name: Wide Pad
programs.description: Saw and pulse ranks spread left and right with a broad chorus. Their different attacks and PWM rates create width while each side retains a useful chord body.

programs.name: Octave Pad
programs.description: A 16' foundation and an 8' upper rank form one true octave. The lighter upper voice arrives later and fades sooner, leaving a rounded low tail.

programs.name: Fifth Pad
programs.description: An 8' root and a quieter 5 1/3' harmonic fifth bloom together. A restrained upper filter crest and little detune keep the open interval clear.

programs.name: Evolving Pad
programs.description: Different rank envelopes evolve into a softly repeating rising filter motion. The 0.7 Hz original SUB supplies the repeating tilt; slow PWM adds an independent movement.

programs.name: Noise Pad
programs.description: A warm pitched saw sustains beneath a separately enveloped band of air. Pressure emphasizes the noise layer; its longer attack and release frame the airy texture.

programs.name: Pressure Pad
programs.description: A soft, dark bed gains most of its level and upper glow from pressure. The body stays warm as the later pulse rank opens; easing pressure lets the chord recede.

programs.name: Sine Pad
programs.description: Pure 8' and quieter 4' sines fade in at different speeds. Pressure shapes their level, not their bypassed filters; no chorus or added hiss clouds the rounded octave.

programs.name: Hollow Pad
programs.description: Near-square pulses emphasize a hollow odd-harmonic center. Shallow, slow width motion and differently filtered ranks soften the sound without making a thin nasal pulse.

programs.name: Resonant Pad
programs.description: A resonant pulse crest opens above a smoother saw body. The upper filter peaks later and decays faster, giving a moving color without both ranks whistling together.

programs.name: Pulse Pad
programs.description: Two pulse-only ranks use distinct PWM rates and depths. A steady low body anchors the moving upper harmonics, with modest chorus instead of excessive pitch detune.

programs.name: Tremolo Pad
programs.description: A warm body and brighter pulse rank share gentle 3.8 Hz SUB amplitude motion. The circuit tremolo adds stereo movement while the whole chord rises and falls smoothly without chopping to silence.

programs.name: Neo-Noir Pad
programs.description: A dark saw foundation supports a later pulse glow, a broad stereo field, chorus and a faint slow ring beat. Long, unequal releases leave a warm cinematic tail after the upper color recedes.

programs.name: Rain Pad
programs.description: An 8 Hz sample-and-hold LFO flickers the filters over a soft pulse body and a little band-limited air. The independent upper envelope lets the airy layer emerge after the pitched body.

programs.name: Cathedral Pad
programs.description: A slow 16' saw foundation carries a quieter 4' sine two octaves above. The clean upper stop enters later; a long dry release suggests space without hidden reverb.

programs.name: Shimmer Pad
programs.description: A soft 8' chord supports a light 2' pulse shimmer. The high rank is deliberately opened for its register and enters late, separating the upper sparkle from the body.

programs.name: Low Drone
programs.description: Stable 16' ranks sustain a deep drone: a rounded saw foundation and a quieter hollow pulse. Slow entry and a long low tail support held bass notes without constant pitch wobble.

programs.name: Ether Pad
programs.description: A pure 8' sine fades in beneath a separate thin veil of filtered noise. The air arrives later and follows pressure more strongly, leaving the pitched center clean and soft.

programs.name: Velvet Pad
programs.description: Softly filtered saw ranks overlap with shallow, unequal blooms. Modest detune and chorus make a dense, smooth chord; the second rank closes earlier on release.

programs.name: Analog Haze
programs.description: A broad saw and moving pulse cloud with deliberately stronger voice variation. Moderate drift and staggered envelopes give a haze while retaining a recognizable chord center.

programs.name: Bowed Glass
programs.description: Slowly entered 8' and 4' sines pass through light fixed-frequency ring modulation. Inharmonic sidebands form a bowed-glass color; pressure grows the tone through its amplitude.

programs.name: Night Pad
programs.description: A dark low-mid saw body appears before a dim pulse halo. Shallow filter movement, a quiet upper layer and long releases keep the sustained chord spacious and subdued.

programs.name: Arctic Pad
programs.description: A thin, bright 8' saw band supports a quiet 4' pulse sheen. Distinct high-pass bands and later upper entry create an icy texture; gently spread ranks supply stereo width under moderate chorus.

programs.name: Poly Stab
programs.description: A dry chord hit with a rounded saw body and shorter bright accent. Both ranks decay away under a held key; velocity controls the bite and level.

programs.name: Poly Brass Stab
programs.description: A brief brass-like opening crest relaxes into a short chord body. The ranks speak at slightly different times and decay fully, giving a compact accented stab.

programs.name: PWM Poly
programs.description: Pulse ranks with separate width rates form a round sustained body and brighter moving edge. The initial accent settles into an animated held chord.

programs.name: Resonant Poly
programs.description: A sharp resonant upper accent sits over a warmer chord body. Unequal filter decay times distinguish the opening bite from the softer held sound.

programs.name: Detuned Poly
programs.description: Full saw ranks beat against each other by 17 cents. The second enters slightly later with a lighter sustain; no chorus masks the direct detuned character.

programs.name: Poly Sweep
programs.description: A quickly established chord opens through staggered filter crests over roughly half a second. Pressure gently brightens the sustain after the opening sweep settles.

programs.name: Velocity Poly
programs.description: Soft strikes stay dark and quiet; hard strikes add substantial level and a bright upper accent. Low static VCA levels make velocity the main dynamic control.

programs.name: Poly Pluck
programs.description: A short bright pulse attack releases into a longer resonant saw body. Both ranks have zero sustain, so held chords decay naturally instead of becoming a pad.

programs.name: Octave Poly
programs.description: A full 8' saw chord carries a lighter 4' crown. The upper filter is opened for its register, and its shorter accent settles without overwhelming the sustained root.

programs.name: Fifth Poly
programs.description: The 8' body and quieter 5 1/3' harmonic fifth form an open chord color. Stable tuning and a lighter sustained upper rank keep the root clear during held voicings.

programs.name: Bright Poly
programs.description: An open saw body and narrow-pulse edge deliver bright, immediate chords. A brief upper accent adds definition while restrained resonance keeps the held sound clear.

programs.name: Dark Poly
programs.description: A filtered saw with a small sine foundation holds the chord beneath a quiet dark pulse. The upper rank closes sooner, leaving a rounded, gently extended release.

programs.name: Hollow Poly
programs.description: Near-square pulses give a hollow, woody chord center. A quieter, slightly narrower upper rank adds a reedy edge; shallow width movement avoids a thin constant sweep.

programs.name: Wide Poly
programs.description: A solid saw and brighter PWM rank spread across the stereo field. Different accent lengths and a broad chorus give width while the sustained chord remains balanced.

programs.name: Poly Swell
programs.description: A soft initial chord grows under pressure. Low static levels leave room for a substantial dynamic swell, and the brighter second rank responds more strongly than the body.

programs.name: Saw Pulse Poly
programs.description: A sustained saw body pairs with a narrower pulse accent. Their distinct spectral and envelope roles remain audible through the short, lightly chorused release.

programs.name: Synthwave Chords
programs.description: Detuned saw chords spread across stereo with a bright opening accent and chorus. The second rank sustains more softly and releases sooner, preserving a warm center in the longer retro tail.

programs.name: Square Poly
programs.description: Unmodulated 50-percent pulses give a clear square-wave chord. The upper rank has a shorter accent and brighter filter; light detune adds body without a PWM sweep.

programs.name: Sine Poly
programs.description: A dominant pure sine body is joined by a small filtered saw attack. The harmonic rank decays to a quiet sustain, leaving rounded chords with meaningful velocity response.

programs.name: Contour Poly
programs.description: A rounded bass-register body opens into clearer upper chords through keyboard brilliance contours. A gentle upper level lift supports melody notes without excessive brightness.

programs.name: Ring Poly
programs.description: A soft saw body and sine-supported pulse edge acquire modest metallic sidebands from the ring modulator. The dry sound retains its pitch and short chord articulation.

programs.name: Glide Poly
programs.description: Sustained saw and pulse chords use gentle polyphonic portamento. Softer onsets let pitch slides speak, while matched rank releases keep the arriving harmony coherent.

programs.name: Tremolo Poly
programs.description: A sustained saw body and softer square rank pulse at 5.4 Hz through the original SUB's VCA route, with a little stereo tremolo color. The opening accent settles quickly so the held chord's rhythmic level motion stays clear.

programs.name: Poly Sub Pulse
programs.description: A 4 Hz square SUB switches between two filter colors on a sustained chord. The lower saw stays present while the resonant pulse emphasizes the rhythmic brightness change.

programs.name: Electric Piano I
programs.description: A warm tine body with individually fading overtones and a velocity-sensitive upper bark. The short strike falls away into a rounded ringing fundamental; key release damps the note.

programs.name: Electric Piano II
programs.description: A covered tine body supports a lighter 4-foot strike with a longer, softer overtone decay than Electric Piano I. Shallow chorus opens the stereo image while the dry attack remains defined.

programs.name: Tine Piano
programs.description: A concentrated tine resonance beneath a separately controlled third-harmonic strike. The struck partials soften at their own rates; the upper rank follows the keyboard and gives firm notes a clear bell-like attack.

programs.name: Clavichord I
programs.description: A dry tangent-excited string spectrum with a short upper snap. Its high partials damp independently, leaving a small clear body; velocity changes the edge as well as the level.

programs.name: Clavichord II
programs.description: A darker tangent string with a shorter, nasal decay. A restrained resonant pulse remains in the attack, while independent upper-partial damping keeps the held tail from becoming an electronic buzz.

programs.name: Funky Clavichord
programs.description: A tangent-string snap and compact resonant wah share the attack. The dry string body adds definition between the filter accents; hard playing brings out the upper rank without leaving a held pad.

programs.name: Harpsichord I
programs.description: A bright quill-plucked string has a notched harmonic spectrum and individually fading upper partials. The short second rank marks the quill release; nearly even strike dynamics and prompt key damping keep the register articulate.

programs.name: Harpsichord II
programs.description: Coupled quill-plucked 8-foot and 4-foot strings with independent harmonic losses. The octave course speaks brightly then recedes, while the lower course rings; the two registers keep nearly even strike dynamics.

programs.name: Lute Harpsichord
programs.description: A covered buff-stop string with rapidly damped upper partials and a restrained quill edge. The low body keeps a definite plucked onset, then settles into a short muted decay with little velocity variation.

programs.name: Toy Piano
programs.description: Small high-register metal modes produce a slightly hollow struck body and brittle upper ping. The bright modes disappear at different rates, leaving a simple ringing center that damps on key release.

programs.name: Honky Keys
programs.description: Two struck-string bodies have controlled upright-like beating and slightly stretched upper partials. Harder notes reveal a firmer hammer spectrum; the detuned ranks decay independently into a warm, uneven shimmer.

programs.name: Vibes Keys
programs.description: A metal-bar body carries independently decaying higher modes, with a separately voiced fourth-harmonic strike. Gentle 5 Hz amplitude motion shades the ringing tail; release damps the body and firm strikes brighten the onset.

programs.name: Celesta
programs.description: A soft hammer excites a clear high-register metal-bar body. Sparse upper modes lose energy independently above the fundamental; the lighter second rank supplies a brief glint without a permanent octave buzz.

programs.name: Saw Pulse Piano
programs.description: A struck-string body joins the deliberately synthetic saw-and-pulse attack. Independent partial losses add a falling piano-like tone beneath the circuit filter motion, retaining the bright electronic character of the name.

programs.name: Soft Keys
programs.description: A felt-like hammer spectrum excites a mellow struck-string body. Upper partials soften quickly while the low body rings, so soft chords remain warm and clear; firmer strikes still open the harmonic color.

programs.name: Chorus Keys
programs.description: A bright tine attack resolves into a smooth electric body with independently softening overtones. Shallow chorus motion shades the long decay while the dry strike keeps chord changes clear.

programs.name: Stage Keys
programs.description: A firm hammer excites a full struck-string spectrum with slight stiffness and controlled unison beating. The bright partials fall away at different rates above a long rounded body; key release damps the strings promptly.

programs.name: Velocity Keys
programs.description: Wide hammer dynamics reveal a soft struck-string body at low velocity and a firm, bright upper attack on hard strikes. Partial-specific losses let the brilliant opening settle naturally instead of leaving a fixed bright tail.

programs.name: Dulcimer
programs.description: A bright hammered steel-string spectrum rings in two courses. Rapidly fading high partials and small pitch beating give way to a clearer lower body; the shorter upper course emphasizes hard mallet strokes.

programs.name: Reed Piano
programs.description: A vibrating-reed spectrum gives hard notes a broad harmonic bark, distinct from a tine bell. The short upper bark falls away into a warmer rounded reed body with partial-specific losses and prompt key-off damping.

programs.name: Glass Keys
programs.description: A clear metal-mode body and brief upper glint create a glassy keyboard texture. Different mode decays evolve inside the shallow chorus, leaving a high, simple ringing tail without held sustain.

programs.name: Tremolo Keys
programs.description: A rounded tine body with a crisp upper strike carries gentle 4.8 Hz full-body tremolo. The upper modes soften independently as the body rings, with restrained stereo color from the chorus/tremolo circuit.

programs.name: Contour Keys
programs.description: A tine-based electric keyboard with a fuller bass and a more present treble strike. Independently damping modes preserve the evolving body across registers; keyboard contour adds level and circuit-brightness contrast.

programs.name: Pressure Keys
programs.description: A struck-string attack settles into a quiet sustaining circuit body. Pressing into the note raises and colors that held bed after the short hammer has faded; the natural-style struck partials provide the onset and initial decay.

programs.name: Flute Organ 8+4
programs.description: An 8' flute-like harmonic registration is supported by a lighter 4' stop. Soft fast gates, straight tuning and velocity-independent sustain keep chord voicings clear, with more body than two pure sines.

programs.name: Flute Organ 16+8
programs.description: A full 16' flute-like harmonic stop supports a lighter 8' registration. The low rank speaks more slowly, and both hold a steady, velocity-independent level without detuning.

programs.name: Percussive Organ
programs.description: An 8' harmonic organ body sustains beneath separate second-harmonic percussion at 4'. The short upper strike fades while the registration remains steady; separated notes retrigger it with no velocity dependence.

programs.name: Reed Organ
programs.description: A steady harmonic registration and pulse edge form a reed-organ color. Distinct bellows-like onsets soften the two 8' ranks, while velocity-independent keying and restrained tuning keep held chords stable.

programs.name: Church Organ
programs.description: A full 16' principal-like harmonic registration supports a restrained 4' flute stop. Differently timed pipe-like entrances preserve the ranks, with a dry release that leaves room for a host hall reverb.

programs.name: Chapel Organ
programs.description: A soft 8' flute-like registration meets a small, quicker-speaking 2' stop. Restrained upper harmonics, gentle pipe speech and compact release suit exposed quiet chords without velocity-driven swells.

programs.name: Theatre Organ
programs.description: Warm 8' and 4' harmonic registrations combine flute body and a restrained reed edge. A gentle 5.6 Hz amplitude tremulant moves the whole registration, with shallow stereo color and steady rank tuning.

programs.name: Tremolo Organ
programs.description: A weighty 16' harmonic flute foundation supports a lighter 4' stop. Gentle 3.2 Hz SUB amplitude motion keeps the low tremolo audible, with restrained stereo color and stable stop tuning.

programs.name: Mellow Organ
programs.description: One rounded 8' registration blends a pure center with a very dark harmonic body. Soft keying, straight pitch and a compact release provide clean accompaniment with no upper stop or velocity-dependent attack.

programs.name: Bright Organ
programs.description: An open 8' principal-like harmonic body carries a small 2' flute stop. Brightness comes from the registration rather than key velocity; crisp gates keep repeated comping clear.

programs.name: Pipe Organ
programs.description: A rounded 16' harmonic foundation meets a brighter 4' principal-like stop. Separate pipe-like onset and release times define the registration without chorus, ensemble detuning or velocity-dependent loudness.

programs.name: Combo Organ
programs.description: A nasal 8' pulse registration and lighter 4' stop preserve the electronic combo-organ character. More open harmonics, a shallower chorus and straighter tuning sharpen rhythmic comping while the keying remains velocity independent.

programs.name: Fifth Organ
programs.description: An 8' harmonic flute registration supports a quieter 5 1/3' quint in the 3:2 ratio. The upper stop stays clearly subordinate to the root, with straight tuning and steady velocity-independent sustain.

programs.name: Organ Vibrato
programs.description: An 8'+4' harmonic flute registration carries restrained 5.9 Hz SUB vibrato. The steady stops retain their clear center and velocity-independent keying while the shallow pitch motion animates held chords.

programs.name: Flute
programs.description: A modeled flute harmonic body carries a separately sustained, quiet air stream. Velocity changes the tongued onset and upper-partial balance; pressure adds breath intensity and restrained vibrato without turning the line into a sine whistle.

programs.name: Breathy Flute
programs.description: A softer modeled flute body supports a stronger, separately sustained air stream. Its cushioned onset and darker harmonics favor quiet phrases; pressure increases breath and body together.

programs.name: Pan Flute
programs.description: A short independent noise chiff leads into a modeled pipe-like harmonic body. The air rank dies away while the held pitch remains; a prompt onset and release keep articulated notes clear.

programs.name: Recorder
programs.description: A clear modeled pipe body is reinforced by quiet odd pulse harmonics and a brief tongue transient. Nearly straight pitch and a short release keep rapid recorder-style phrasing articulate.

programs.name: Clarinet
programs.description: A modeled clarinet body emphasizes the hollow odd harmonics while allowing a restrained register-dependent upper edge. A separate short tongue and breath rank support the onset; pressure increases reed intensity without broad pitch wobble.

programs.name: Bass Clarinet
programs.description: A 16' clarinet body uses a larger bore geometry and a lower register transition, retaining a woody fundamental beneath a quieter upper reed band. The softer breath onset and restrained pressure vibrato keep low-register phrases clear.

programs.name: Oboe
programs.description: A focused modeled double-reed spectrum combines a strong nasal center with a smaller upper edge. The ranks speak at slightly different times; velocity sharpens the tongue while pressure changes harmonic intensity during the hold.

programs.name: English Horn
programs.description: A larger double-reed body shifts the resonant bands downward while keeping the played pitch intact. Its rounded fundamental, broader articulation and gentler nasal edge distinguish the voice from Oboe even at the same sounding note.

programs.name: Bassoon
programs.description: A 16' modeled bassoon spectrum pairs a woody low body with a smaller nasal overtone band. The definite tongue and compact release keep low lines separated, while pressure adds body and controlled reed brightness.

programs.name: Soprano Reed
programs.description: A bright modeled reed body supports a lighter narrow-pulse upper band. A restrained onset scoop and stable tuning keep upper-register lines focused; pressure supplies harmonic brightness and a small vibrato.

programs.name: Ocarina
programs.description: A soft 4' vessel-like body retains a nearly pure fundamental with very restrained modeled harmonics. A trace of separate air and a rounded onset keep the line alive, with no lower pitched rank mixed in.

programs.name: Piccolo
programs.description: An agile 2' modeled flute body carries a bright, controlled harmonic edge and a short independent air onset. Both ranks remain in the high register; quick articulation keeps the piccolo-like line clear.

programs.name: Whistle
programs.description: A nearly pure 4' whistle gains a trace of moving pipe harmonics beneath a gentle onset rise. The second rank stays out of the mix; a short glide, responsive level and restrained vibrato keep the line focused.

programs.name: Shakuhachi
programs.description: A modeled flute body follows an aspirated attack that settles quickly to quiet breath. A controlled upward onset bend and pressure-driven harmonic intensity distinguish the phrase from a static noise-and-sine blend.

programs.name: Guitar I
programs.description: A nylon-like plucked-string spectrum has a warm body and a brief finger/pick edge. The excitation notch and faster high-partial losses let the clear lower string outlast the attack; harder playing brightens the strike.

programs.name: Guitar II
programs.description: A brighter steel-string body carries a firmer pick and longer upper shimmer than Guitar I. Independently damping partials soften the attack naturally above the ringing lower string.

programs.name: Funky Pluck I
programs.description: A compact tangent-string snap joins a fast resonant filter attack. Independent upper losses clarify repeated notes while the circuit pulse retains the dry, rhythmic wah character.

programs.name: Funky Pluck II
programs.description: A more open plucked-string body sits inside the slower wah-shaped circuit contour. The brief upper snap marks the strike, then independently damping string partials leave a rounded, expressive tail.

programs.name: Harp
programs.description: A finger-plucked harp string excites a rounded soundboard response with a broad, softly notched upper spectrum. The short contact rank shares the string's pitch, then yields to a long lower aftersound. Soft arpeggios retain their gentler attack and can ring across key releases.

programs.name: Koto
programs.description: A near-bridge plectrum opens a bright notched string spectrum over the koto's long-board response. A quiet short contact rank shares the played pitch; upper string modes soften before the ringing body. Restrained initial settling leaves the ribbon available for deliberate bends.

programs.name: Banjo
programs.description: A sharp string pluck excites the banjo's membrane-and-bridge response, with a strong low-mid body and a dry bright edge. Fast losses around the head resonance let the sound clear between picked notes; the brief contact rank adds no unrelated clavichord or held oscillator buzz.

programs.name: Mandolin
programs.description: Two close steel-string courses ring with independent partial losses and a restrained pitch offset. Their bright paired attacks stay compact; repeated strikes create tremolo picking while the paired courses retain gentle beating between strokes.

programs.name: Drone Pluck
programs.description: A bright string strike recedes into a quiet resonant drone with faint ring color. Independently damping plucked partials animate the opening; pressure raises the remaining circuit bed after the upper pick disappears.

programs.name: Nylon Pluck
programs.description: A warm plucked nylon-string spectrum carries a soft finger attack and clear lower body. The excitation notch and fast upper-partial damping keep the sound round as it decays, without chorus or detuning.

programs.name: Steel Pluck
programs.description: Paired 8-foot and 4-foot steel-string courses open with bright, independently fading harmonics. The octave course recedes before the full lower body, with a tiny tuning offset adding restrained beating.

programs.name: Muted Pluck
programs.description: A palm-muted string spectrum carries a brief pick click and a rounded low note. Fast partial losses and short body damping make repeated strokes distinct even while the keys stay held.

programs.name: Kalimba
programs.description: A thumb-plucked supported tine gives a rounded fundamental and a brief nonharmonic ping, distinct from an electric-piano pickup. Both ranks share the played pitch; the brighter contact fades first while the lower tine continues ringing after key release.

programs.name: Zither
programs.description: Two bright steel-string courses have long unequal body decays and independent upper-partial losses. A restrained pitch offset and shallow chorus add a gentle ensemble shimmer after the clearly plucked onset.

programs.name: Dulcimer Pluck
programs.description: A firm steel-string pluck has a bright short octave course and a longer lower body. Upper modes lose energy independently, leaving a clear ringing string after the plectrum edge has faded.

programs.name: Pressure Pluck
programs.description: A natural-style picked string onset settles over a quiet held circuit bed. The high string modes fade independently; pressure swells and colors the remaining body after the short pick has disappeared.

programs.name: Analog Bass
programs.description: A firm 16-foot saw-and-sine body carries a brisk, separately decaying 8-foot pulse edge. A cleaner low sustain and more gradual filter settling give repeated notes weight without leaving an abrasive upper buzz.

programs.name: Resonance Bass
programs.description: A fast resonant upper sweep settles above a firm sine-supported low note. The body opens more slowly than the edge, keeping the attack lively while the low sustain remains focused.

programs.name: Sine Bass
programs.description: A rounded 16-foot sine takes over from a very brief, velocity-sensitive upper click. A slower low-frequency onset and quicker click release reduce mechanical edges while the held fundamental stays clean and steady.

programs.name: Sub Bass
programs.description: A centered 16-foot sine has a smooth low-frequency onset, useful touch dynamics and a tightly controlled ending. Keyboard level contour gently restrains the lowest notes while the pure sustaining body remains stable.

programs.name: Pluck Bass
programs.description: A plucked-string spectrum joins the compact resonant low body. The upper pick decays first and high string partials soften independently, leaving a clearly pitched low tail that fully dies on a held key.

programs.name: Fretless Glide
programs.description: A soft fingered string spectrum sings through a long low decay. Independent partial losses soften the note after the onset; short portamento joins phrases and pressure adds restrained vibrato and a singing upper edge.

programs.name: Funk Bass
programs.description: A dry fingered-string snap sits inside a tight resonant filter pluck. Hard strikes expose the brief upper edge; independently damping string partials keep the low body defined between rhythmic notes.

programs.name: Brass Bass
programs.description: A solid 16-foot saw body opens into an 8-foot brass spectrum. Unequal attack and filter blooms separate the low support from the lip-like upper accent; pressure opens the held brass color without loosening the foundation.

programs.name: Octave Bass
programs.description: A firm lower saw and a separately shaped octave retain two audible registers. The upper attack relaxes into a controlled sustain while the low rank settles more slowly, adding movement without detuning the bass.

programs.name: Pulse Bass
programs.description: Two low pulses move with independently paced shallow PWM above a stable sine foundation. A compact upper onset and calmer held harmonic balance keep the width motion clear without softening the bass center.

programs.name: Round Bass
programs.description: A soft fingered-string component adds a gentle falling articulation to the warm sustaining sine-and-saw body. A quiet same-register edge supplies definition while low resonance keeps the bass rounded.

programs.name: Velocity Bass
programs.description: Soft strikes expose a covered low body while hard strikes bring out a much brighter, shorter upper attack. The two filter and amplitude contours settle at different rates, keeping the struck dynamic distinct in a phrase.

programs.name: Rubber Bass
programs.description: A brief upward pitch scoop lands on a rounded resonant pluck. A small string-like component strengthens the initial note center while both ranks decay completely, avoiding a permanent sustain or ongoing pitch wobble.

programs.name: Dark Bass
programs.description: A deep sine-supported body has a covered same-register saw shadow and a softly falling string component. The restrained upper spectrum preserves pitch clarity while a smooth onset and short release keep the dark bass controlled.

programs.name: Bright Bass
programs.description: A full low saw body supports a clear, velocity-sensitive upper saw edge. The brighter rank decays into a restrained sustain, leaving a firm foundation beneath the articulate attack.

programs.name: Picked Bass
programs.description: A short, firm pick excites a low string spectrum with independent harmonic losses. The upper pick vanishes quickly while the fundamental and lower modes continue ringing, then damp promptly on key release.

programs.name: Upright Pluck
programs.description: A rounded low string spectrum has a woody finger onset and a gently falling body. Independently damping upper partials leave a clear fundamental, while a small circuit-noise transient supplies a brief finger-and-string texture.

programs.name: Fifth Bass
programs.description: A stable low foundation supports a quieter upper twelfth. Its upper rank speaks briefly at the strike, then settles into a lean harmonic support, making the fifth clear without masking the bass fundamental.

programs.name: Pedal Bass
programs.description: Steady low and octave sine stops use rounded keying and closely controlled releases. A gentle low-key level contour restrains boom; velocity remains neutral so held organ-style bass lines stay even.

programs.name: Squelch Bass
programs.description: A sharply resonant upper contour sweeps into a compact sine-supported bass. The upper accent closes rapidly while the lower filter settles more gradually, preserving a firm note center under the squelch.

programs.name: Ring Bass
programs.description: A centered low body feeds a light 35 Hz ring growl beneath a narrower upper attack. Unequal filter settling and restrained upper sustain keep the moving sidebands textured while the dry bass remains clear.

programs.name: Sub Wobble Bass
programs.description: A 3 Hz filter movement animates the upper pulse layer while a stable bypass sine supports the bass. A more compact onset and separated rank contours keep the rhythmic motion clear without pitch wobble.

programs.name: Pressure Bass
programs.description: A firm sine-supported note speaks immediately, with a soft falling string detail at the onset. Pressure then raises the brighter upper circuit rank and opens its spectrum, keeping the low center steady as the phrase grows.

programs.name: Contour Bass
programs.description: A dry saw-and-pulse bass has a restrained low-key level and a clearer upper-register attack. Different rank decays and keyboard brightness contour keep fast runs articulated without adding pitch instability.

programs.name: Touch Lead
programs.description: A firm saw body with a lighter pulse edge. Velocity shapes the onset; pressure adds level, brilliance and gentle vibrato. The wheel supplies additional controlled vibrato.

programs.name: Aftertouch Vibrato Lead
programs.description: A centered, singing lead whose vibrato grows with pressure to roughly a quarter-tone peak-to-peak. The quiet dry tone is stable; pressure supplies most of the expressive level and vibrato, while velocity gives a smaller onset contrast.

programs.name: Ribbon Glide Lead
programs.description: A smooth, centered lead for ribbon gestures. Short portamento and a small upward onset scoop connect phrases; a restrained upper edge keeps large slides readable.

programs.name: Noir Lead
programs.description: A dark saw body blooms into a later brass edge. Pressure opens the sustained tone and adds controlled vibrato; moderate chorus and a long release support spacious single lines.

programs.name: Neo-Noir Brass Lead
programs.description: A dark harmonic brass body supports a slower saw-and-pulse bloom and a sustained release. Pressure brings out the brighter crown while moderate detune supplies width.

programs.name: Glide Lead
programs.description: A steady saw-and-pulse tone with long, smooth portamento between notes. Gentle envelope motion keeps the glide audible without adding an onset pitch scoop.

programs.name: Sine Lead
programs.description: One pure 8' sine with a rounded onset. Pressure controls level and a gentle vibrato; filter brilliance is intentionally inactive on this bypass-sine voice.

programs.name: Whistle Lead
programs.description: A single 4' sine with a small upward scoop and quick breath-like articulation. Pressure adds restrained vibrato and level; no lower-octave rank is mixed in.

programs.name: Square Lead
programs.description: A hollow 8' square body with a quieter same-register square edge. Nearly unison tuning and dry, quick articulation preserve the centered odd-harmonic character.

programs.name: Narrow Pulse Lead
programs.description: A narrow pulse body with a lighter, differently voiced pulse edge. The dry, nasal tone has a clear attack and restrained vibrato for agile lines.

programs.name: Resonant Lead
programs.description: A moving resonant edge above a warmer body. Pressure raises the filter focus while modest low-cut settings retain a pitched foundation.

programs.name: Screaming Lead
programs.description: A focused, aggressive upper resonance responds strongly to pressure. A quieter saw-and-sine body holds the pitch beneath the brighter edge; vibrato stays controlled.

programs.name: Fifth Lead
programs.description: An 8' body with a lighter 5 1/3' rank at a harmonic fifth. The upper voice has its own brighter filter and slower onset, preserving clarity in the interval.

programs.name: Octave Lead
programs.description: A solid 8' saw under a sustained 4' pulse crown. The octave has a higher cutoff and a lighter level, so its presence stays clear without taking over the lead.

programs.name: Soft Lead
programs.description: A rounded saw-and-sine body with a quiet soft pulse edge. Gently staggered attacks and restrained pressure brightness keep slow phrases warm and centered.

programs.name: Init Bend Lead
programs.description: A clear upward scoop begins below each struck note and settles quickly into a bright sustained lead. Harder strikes deepen the scoop; there is no constant pitch modulation.

programs.name: Pressure Lead
programs.description: Requires poly or channel aftertouch: hold a key and press to bring the sound out of silence. On screen, drag down on a held key. Pressure controls level and brightness; releasing pressure fades the tone.

programs.name: Velocity Lead
programs.description: Strike velocity controls a wide range of level and brightness. The quiet static gain lets soft notes stay soft, while hard strikes reveal a more prominent pulse edge.

programs.name: Detuned Lead
programs.description: Two sustained saw ranks with a deliberate 12-cent offset. Their different filters and attacks create a broad beating lead without added chorus or deep pressure vibrato.

programs.name: Sub Vibrato Lead
programs.description: A smooth lead with a continuous, restrained 5.2 Hz vibrato. Pressure adds a small amount of depth and level, allowing the held tone to sing without a wide pitch wobble.

programs.name: Trill Lead
programs.description: A square SUB alternates approximately one semitone below and above the played pitch at 6 Hz. Pressure and wheel pitch routes are disabled so the interval remains deliberate.

programs.name: Glissando Lead
programs.description: A clearly articulated lead whose portamento steps through semitones. The steady sustain and simple filter motion keep the discrete glissando easy to hear.

programs.name: Brass Lead
programs.description: A compact circuit brass body is supported by a harmonic lip spectrum, then a brighter saw edge. The short accent settles into a centered sustain; velocity controls breath effort and pressure adds bloom. Separate short releases keep single lines clear.

programs.name: Reed Lead
programs.description: A focused clarinet-like harmonic body meets a quieter double-reed and pulse edge. A definite tongue onset and short breath release keep lines dry and articulate; pressure adds nasal intensity and restrained vibrato without removing the fundamental.

programs.name: Wah Lead
programs.description: Pressure brings a 3.8 Hz SUB sine into the resonant filter route. The unpressed note stays centered; leaning in adds a rhythmic wah without also creating pitch vibrato.

programs.name: Ring Lead
programs.description: A clean center tone mixed with 280 Hz ring sidebands for a metallic edge. The restrained wet blend preserves pitch identity while pressure brightens the source.

programs.name: Hollow Lead
programs.description: A near-square body and a quieter moving pulse create a hollow tone with slow harmonic motion. The lower-width body stays stable while the second rank carries most of the PWM.

programs.name: Ether Lead
programs.description: One 8' sine with a soft onset, long glide and expressive pressure level. Gentle pressure vibrato gives a theremin-like gesture without an unintended beating second oscillator.

programs.name: Solo Synth
programs.description: A bright, agile saw lead with a lightly supporting pulse edge. Quick articulation, useful velocity contrast and modest pressure vibrato suit exposed melodic lines.

programs.name: Contour Lead
programs.description: A rounded lower register opens progressively into brighter upper notes. A gentle high-key level trim balances that added brilliance while retaining clear solo articulation.

programs.name: Ring Bell I
programs.description: A clear bell body with independently fading metal modes feeds the fixed 307 Hz ring carrier. The short octave strike and velocity-sensitive impact open into a long, evolving metallic tail.

programs.name: Ring Bell II
programs.description: A darker modal bell body and a bright upper twelfth feed the lower 191 Hz ring carrier. Fast upper-mode losses produce a sharper clang and more covered tail than Ring Bell I.

programs.name: Tubular Bells
programs.description: A struck tube carries a weak low spectrum and a bright octave nominal, with the near 2:3:4 upper group suggesting the played pitch. The separate hard contact shares the same tube tuning, then clears to leave its independently decaying metal modes.

programs.name: Glockenspiel
programs.description: A hard, high-register metal-bar strike excites sparse inharmonic modes that track each key. The brightest modes fall away first above a clear ringing pitch; the upper rank adds a tiny hard-mallet accent.

programs.name: Celeste Bells
programs.description: A soft hammer excites a delicate metal-bar spectrum with an independently fading upper accent. Gentle chorus shades the modal decay while the unmodulated pitch remains clear; key release damps the small ringing bars.

programs.name: Music Box
programs.description: A small plucked comb tooth rings with a clear high pitch and sparse upper resonances near 6.27 times its fundamental. A short same-pitch contact glint lights the attack; the bright overtones fade into the simple mechanical ringing tail.

programs.name: Gong
programs.description: A low mallet thud opens into a dense, irregular set of plate modes. Delayed upper resonances bloom after the impact, then lose energy at different rates; the same tuned plate supplies the strike and the lingering, shifting aftersound.

programs.name: Temple Bell
programs.description: A deep struck shell rings with stable close mode pairs and slow metallic beating. Widely separated upper resonances recede from the initial clang, leaving a calm low aftersound; the brief hard contact and the long body share one shell pitch.

programs.name: Marimba
programs.description: A wooden-bar spectrum carries a soft fundamental and quickly damped higher modes. A separate brief fourth-harmonic mallet knock supplies the strike; hard playing opens the upper wood color without a ring carrier.

programs.name: Vibraphone
programs.description: A long metal-bar body carries unequal higher-mode decays and a separately controlled fourth-harmonic strike. Smooth 5.2 Hz tremolo moves the full resonance while a continuous pitched body remains between the crests. Key release closes the damper; the sustain control can hold the resonance.

programs.name: Xylophone
programs.description: A hard high-register wooden bar carries a strong third harmonic, with a bright opening and compact pitched decay. Fast independent losses remove the upper knock early, keeping repeated notes dry and distinct.

programs.name: Crystal Bell
programs.description: Bright tracked metal modes feed a glassy ring color beneath the brittle upper strike. Unequal modal decays reveal a clear high body as the brilliant impact disappears.

programs.name: Bell Pad
programs.description: A struck modal upper edge dissolves into a quiet sustained bell-and-sine bed. Slowly changing partial balance, shallow chorus and unequal releases support chords without holding the initial clang at a fixed brightness.

programs.name: Ring Sweep Bell
programs.description: A fast carrier sweep crosses the inharmonic modes at impact, then falls over the ringing body. Independent modal losses and a short upper strike keep the moving tail distinct from the initial clang.

programs.name: Steel Drum
programs.description: A struck steel shell carries a tuned octave and twelfth above the fundamental. A rounded mallet contact gives way to independently fading shell modes; each note retains its pitched center without a fixed carrier.

programs.name: Chimes
programs.description: High struck metal modes and a quieter octave course ring with unequal long decays. The opening glint falls away into clear tracked resonances without unrelated fixed-carrier sidebands.

programs.name: Dark Bell
programs.description: A low modal resonance supports a subdued short upper strike. The dark body loses its highest modes quickly, then leaves a long low tail with restrained ring color instead of a bright metallic wash.

programs.name: Bell Choir
programs.description: Two tracked modal bells sound a fifth apart, with different brightness and decay. The upper bell recedes earlier while light chorus and a restrained ring blend join the remaining resonances.

programs.name: Metallic Keys
programs.description: A hard reed-like strike and modal metal body retain a deliberately synthetic ring edge. Fast high-partial decay takes the initial clang away before the pitched tail, while the residual filtered saw keeps the texture forward.

programs.name: Agogo
programs.description: A small hollow bell opens with a hard contact and several widely spaced metal resonances. Its compact shell damps quickly for repeated strokes; a short same-pitch upper knock adds definition to each crisp metal hit.

programs.name: Clock Bells
programs.description: Two clear modal bells at 4-foot and 2-2/3-foot pitch sound a true fifth apart. A concise upper impact yields to unequal ringing decays with no fixed-carrier interference.

programs.name: Ring Mallet
programs.description: A rounded wooden-mode body supports a short metallic upper mallet, then feeds the ring circuit. Hard strikes expose the upper clang; its rapid losses leave a softer resonating body behind.

programs.name: Random Filter
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold steps the resonant filters at 7.5 Hz. A saw body and lighter octave pulse make each held random cutoff audible as a computer-like burble.

programs.name: Random Pitch Blips
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold picks small, unquantized pitch steps around the played key at 6.5 Hz. A matching square amplitude LFO separates the sine-and-pulse tone into blips.

programs.name: Siren
programs.description: A sine body and quiet octave harmonic follow a smooth three-semitone peak-to-peak SUB wail. Rounded onset and release avoid clicks; pressure quickens the siren.

programs.name: Laser Zap
programs.description: A resonant pulse sweep drops sharply after the strike, with no bypass sine masking the descent. A separate, very short noise flash adds the laser's initial snap.

programs.name: Wind
programs.description: An airy gust enters before the broad low wind bed. Independently paced smooth random filter and level motion forms uneven gusts, without a repeating SUB pulse; pressure raises the upper air, which subsides before the low bed.

programs.name: Surf
programs.description: One breaking wave unfolds per note: the low surge rises first, brighter spray blooms later, and the foam drains away ahead of the long low wash. Independent one-shot envelopes shape the wave without a cyclic amplitude or filter pulse.

programs.name: Sci-Fi Drone
programs.description: A dark 16' saw-and-sine foundation supports a later third-harmonic pulse. Slow ring beating and gentle filter drift animate the held drone without a sharp attack.

programs.name: Robot Voice
programs.description: A voiced ah-formant body carries a fixed 73 Hz mechanical ring, with a brief noisy saw consonant above it. The vocal resonances retain their shape across pitch changes; pressure opens and raises the sustained robotic vowel.

programs.name: Alarm
programs.description: A clear 4' call alternates between two pitches three semitones apart. A quieter low pulse gives the onset weight while square SUB level motion accents the two-tone warning.

programs.name: Space Sweep
programs.description: A low body and later upper pulse bloom as the ring carrier rises, then falls over several seconds. Different filter and amplitude swells make the motion unfold in layers.

programs.name: Bubbles
programs.description: An 11 Hz sample-and-hold source picks resonant bubble colors while two independent smooth random level contours make the pops uneven in strength. A hollow pulse body and a little filtered noise keep their separate rounded and airy edges.

programs.name: Thunder
programs.description: A brief broadband crack precedes a slower low rumble with a long falling tail. Smooth random intensity and spectral changes make the roll uneven without periodic pumping; broad low resonance avoids a fixed pitched boom, and velocity controls the impact.

programs.name: Rain
programs.description: A continuous rain bed supports fine upper droplets. Fast raised-cosine random intensity contours combine with independent slower filter and level movement, keeping the rainfall fluid rather than switching the whole bed in clocked steps.

programs.name: Helicopter
programs.description: A low 16' pulse engine and a separate rotor-noise band throb at 11.5 Hz. SUB level and filter pulses leave the underlying engine audible; pressure accelerates the rotor.

programs.name: UFO Landing
programs.description: A low sine body follows repeating downward SUB glides while the shared ring carrier settles over the phrase. Release all keys and any sustain hold before the next attack to restart that sweep; a shorter upper pulse edge marks each note.

programs.name: Telemetry
programs.description: A high narrow pulse alternates pitches at 7 Hz, with a sharper 2' onset edge. Brief release and shallow level pulses keep the electronic signal dry and articulated.

programs.name: Clockwork
programs.description: Six-Hz retriggered envelopes make short mechanical ticks from a high pulse and thin noise edge. Each tick falls silent before the next; slower SUB filter steps alternate the tick-tock color, and held chords cycle through their keyed pitches.

programs.name: Deep Space
programs.description: A very slow 16' sine bloom carries a later, cloudy noise band. Gentle sub-hertz ring beating and long independent releases leave a deep, moving tail.

programs.name: Metal Scrape
programs.description: A resonant saw-and-noise body follows a short high noise scrape. The ring carrier falls quickly after impact, adding a rough metallic edge to the closing filter bands.

programs.name: Machine Hum
programs.description: A steady 16' pulse motor supports a quieter upper mechanical buzz. A fixed 50 Hz ring carrier supplies sidebands, with a gradual start and a short coast after release.

programs.name: Sweep Riser
programs.description: Hold a note for a long resonant rise: the low saw opens broadly before the later noise crest blooms above it. The slower filter entrance and restrained resonance keep the rising band defined without an abrupt early whistle; its peak settles gradually.

programs.name: Downer
programs.description: A bright held saw falls into a low filter setting when the key is released. The longer body release keeps that downward sweep audible after the shorter noisy upper edge fades.

programs.name: Glitch Sub
programs.description: Thirty-Hz SUB filter steps roughen a low pulse into a digital-sounding buzz. A shorter upper saw edge marks each keystroke, while shallow level pulses reinforce the flutter.

programs.name: Breath FX
programs.description: A soft low breath band supports a faster upper-air layer. Pressure raises the airy rank more strongly and gently opens both filters, giving a controllable exhale and fade.

programs.name: Delay Brass
programs.description: Play clipped midrange chords; a defined brass body and shorter lip accent leave gaps for 375 ms echoes. Pressure develops the held spectrum while the short dry releases keep phrases clear.

programs.name: Plate Pad
programs.description: Hold open chords around C3-C5; a soft lower pulse blooms beneath an octave sheen. Release between changes to hear the warm plate tail.

programs.name: Phaser Strings
programs.description: Bow connected chords in C3-C5 and hold phrase endings. A clear bowed body and quieter, later pulse edge expose the phaser notches while keeping a steady pitch center.

programs.name: Drive Lead
programs.description: Play firm lines in C4-C6: a pulse body carries a shorter saw edge into warm drive. Pressure adds bite and restrained vibrato.

programs.name: Arp Poly
programs.description: Hold two to four notes around C3-C4 for eight notes per second across two octaves. A short octave accent and one-second filter cycle articulate the ascent.

programs.name: Arp Bells
programs.description: Hold a small chord around C4 for four notes per second, rising and falling over two octaves. A short third-harmonic strike leaves space for 375 ms echoes.

programs.name: Arp Bass
programs.description: Hold a root and fifth around C3 for a six-note-per-second bass pattern. A compact 16' body and short 8' snap follow a gentle four-step filter cycle.

programs.name: LFO Sweep Pad
programs.description: Hold spacious chords for at least ten seconds. A broad triangle filter sweep moves over a warm low body, with slower irregular stereo drift.

programs.name: LFO Pan Keys
programs.description: Play relaxed C3-C6 chords and let them ring. A tine body changes color with velocity and rocks left to right once per second; its separate high-passed octave strike fades first.

programs.name: PWM LFO Strings
programs.description: Sustain midrange chords: two differently biased pulse ranks share a slow triangle width sweep. The later, brighter rank adds a gentle shimmer.

programs.name: Stereo Delay Pluck
programs.description: Play sparse picked figures around C3-C5. A resonant steel-string body and short high-passed octave pick feed 250 ms stereo echoes; lift early for clean gaps.

programs.name: Ambient Bells
programs.description: Strike widely spaced notes around C4-C6 and allow the decay to clear. A rounded fundamental outlasts the upper fifth; quiet 560 ms echoes open into a dark plate.

programs.name: Ensemble Plus
programs.description: Use open midrange voicings and sustain through the staggered bow onset. Differently sized string bodies, restrained original chorus and a shallow three-tap ensemble widen the sound while keeping its center clear.

programs.name: Space Lead
programs.description: Connect single lines in C4-C6 with short slides and leave room for 400 ms echoes. Pressure introduces gentle vibrato; the dry release keeps phrase endings clear.

programs.name: Random Arp
programs.description: Hold a small chord near C3 for six random notes per second over two octaves. Sample-and-hold brightness changes at half the note rate; short releases separate the notes.

programs.name: Drive Bass
programs.description: Play short bass lines around C3. A firm 16' pulse-and-sine body anchors a brief 8' rasp; firmer strikes add level and bite, while parallel drive gently smooths the edge.

programs.name: Phased Polysynth
programs.description: Use compact rhythmic chords in C3-C5. A broad saw body follows a sharper pulse accent; the phaser animates the held tail, with a short plate after release.

programs.name: Tremolo LFO Organ
programs.description: Hold chords around C3-C5 for a steady four-pulse-per-second tremolo. The 8' body has a little reed edge; pressure brings forward the sustained 4' stop.

programs.name: Init Circuit
programs.description: A clean starting point on the circuit engine: one saw rank, open filter, no modulation.
